SPEC LINK: docs/specs/02-web-admin/126_maxbld_surface_standard.md §3, §4 (the 21 categories) · §128 R-02 (archetype gates fields), R-13 (owns.components), R-16 ("none" carries a why), R-34 (ad policy is checks[], never plausibility[]). EVERY category below answers from a CLOSED menu, on the step.schema.json idiom: "none" is a legal ANSWER and never a legal omission; every enum value carries its meaning in its own description; every answer carries a `why` and an `evidence` list. "UNRESEARCHED" is a first-class value on every vocabulary so an unresearched estate is COUNTABLE rather than blank — docs/reports/generated/127-surface-registry.md renders the count per row and in its summary. Under Spec 122 R2 the SCHEMA is canonical and prose menus are generated FROM it; that applies here the moment this file is ratified. Ratification is Phase 1. DO NOT set x-frozen true without the freeze artifact and its lock (Spec 124 R-X). ONE SOURCE RULE: this schema is the single source. From it come the TypeScript types (src/lib/surfaces/generated/surface-descriptor.d.ts), the runtime validator the engine and the tests share, the migration assertions, the API contracts, the web/mobile/admin projections, the generated registry, and the Supabase seed. Nothing downstream is hand-written, and nothing downstream is a second declaration. DRAFT SENTINEL: a field marked `x-draft-optional: true` may carry the literal "UNRESEARCHED" while the estate is being researched. The registry counts every one of them. No other field may.

programme.description: WHICH PROGRAMME this entry belongs to. Without it the registry is an undifferentiated list of 137 things and a reader cannot tell the parcel cost tool from the lead-gen estate it happens to share a repository with.

oneOf.description: The MaxBLD parcel cost tool ITSELF — the surfaces, contracts, tables and jobs a customer touches, plus the five business requirements that hang off it: the metered lookup, the PDF sent to a client, the ad placements, and the Vercel web front door. Governed by Spec 100 and Spec 126; this is the programme.

The admin surfaces that OPERATE the parcel product — usage and entitlements, placements and advertiser accounts, the PDF audit, the app_outputs recompute, and the descriptor-native registry/drift/roles pages. Governed by Spec 126; converts with the product, not after it.

Used by BOTH products and owned by neither: auth, the user profile, the subscription and Stripe hand-off, entitlements, notifications, and the navigation shells. Converting one of these changes both products, which is why it is its own scope rather than being filed under whichever one noticed it first.

The OTHER product — lead generation, the flight center, the lead feed, permit and job detail, builders and entities. INVENTORIED ONLY. It is fenced from the parcel tool by Spec 128 R-03, it converts under the same standard in a later programme, and it appears here so that a shared contract or an orphan is visible rather than hidden.

tracked-lots (parcel_product) — Keep an eye on specific lots: the user’s own saved parcels, their envelope figures, and whether a CoA ruling has landed near them. Its own feature module so it is removable as a unit — one table, one contract, one surface — and so it shares nothing with the lead-gen save machinery (Spec 116 OD5).

flight-center (estate_other) — The job board and job detail. The other product.
permits-builders-entities (estate_other) — Permit, builder and entity data serving lead-gen.
scheduled-jobs (estate_other) — Cron jobs and CI workflows with no product owner.

build_order.description: DERIVED, not chosen: scope rank (A<B<C<D) × 1000 + feature rank × 10 + kind rank, where kind rank orders tables-before-contracts-before-surfaces-before-admin. It answers "what must exist before this can be built", and it is the order the review queue renders in.

leakage.description: Behaviour inside this row that belongs to the OTHER product and merely lives here today. Recorded, NEVER deleted: a behaviour nobody wrote down is a behaviour nobody can knowingly retire (Spec 124 §4, the Chesterton's-Fence rule).

allOf.x-profile: LIST — a scrollable collection. render.list (item archetype, pagination, recycling) is REQUIRED, as are inputs.contract_ref and states.
DETAIL — one entity by id. inputs.query_key must be single-param (Spec 99 §4 hygiene, as schema); states must include error.
REPORT — read-only. outputs and state are FORCED to "none"; inputs.field_whitelist is REQUIRED and must equal the contract's; plausibility and render.targets are declared.
SEARCH — a query box. config.debounce_ms, config.min_query_len and guards.rate_bucket are REQUIRED; never log the raw query.
FORM — writes user input. outputs.contract_ref and outputs.rollback are REQUIRED; state.fields carry the Spec 99 §3 row as data.
WIZARD_STEP — one ordered step. render.wizard (step_index, advances_on, resume_key, skip_when, terminal) is REQUIRED.
DASHBOARD — tiles that degrade independently. render.tiles and render.refresh are REQUIRED — a tile grid with no per-tile degradation is the measured DataQualityDashboard defect.

GATE — renders a block instead of content. guards.statuses_handled is REQUIRED and must cover every value of the closed set it gates on. outputs.answer is narrowed to none | device_only | contract_only — AMENDED 2026-09-15 from a blanket "none" after research measured three legitimate writers: an auth-confirm screen writing a session to on-device storage, a permission modal registering a push token, and the paywall POSTing a checkout session. What a GATE may never do is write optimistically or write the database directly.
SLOT — a sponsored placement. offers may NOT be "none"; its disclosure carries severity FAIL and blocking true as SEPARATE fields (R-17/R-34); outputs forced "none".

STATIC — content or a redirect. outputs.answer forced "none"; state.answer narrowed to none | mmkv — AMENDED 2026-09-15 after research measured the offline banner caching its last connectivity state on device. A STATIC surface still fetches nothing.
SHELL — a navigation container. render.routing.branches is REQUIRED — a shell here is NOT inert; one is the sole subscription gate for five tabs and another the sole routing authority.
kind SURFACE takes only a SURFACE archetype.
kind CONTRACT takes only a CONTRACT archetype, and renders nothing.
kind JOB takes only a JOB archetype, and has no platform.
